source.original_text:
ASTIS-authored canonical analytic lemma, not a verbatim textbook theorem or the complete source exercise.
Let E be any complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let mu be any measure. Suppose f:E→R is genuinely C2, f and its true gradient belong to L2(mu), and f² log(f²) is integrable. Let chi_R be the existing radial smooth cutoff at radius R, and set f_n=chi_(n+1)*f. Then the integrals of f_n², f_n² log(f_n²), and ||gradient f_n||² converge respectively to those of f², f² log(f²), and ||gradient f||². Finite dimension, probability, finite total measure, positivity and nonzero function mass are not required.

lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (μ : Measure E) (f : E → ℝ),
    ContDiff ℝ 2 f → MemLp f 2 μ → MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ →
    Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2)) μ →
    let fn := fun n : ℕ => fun x : E => radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) x * f x
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂μ)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 * Real.log ((fn n x)^2) ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2) ∂μ)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, ‖gradient (fn n) x‖^2 ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂μ))

decoder_context: The carriers and typeclasses have their usual Mathlib meanings: a real inner-product normed additive group, its compatible Borel measurable structure, and completeness. FiniteDimensional is present only where the displayed type says so.
ContDiff real 2 means globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable; the smooth infinity notation means C-infinity, not the distinct analytic omega order.
gradient is the literal Hilbert Riesz inverse of the real Frechet derivative of the given function. It is not an arbitrary supplied field or a chosen Radon-Nikodym representative.

MemLp g 2 mu means a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm; Integrable h mu means actual a.e. strong measurability and finite integral of the norm. Every integral displayed here is a real Bochner integral with respect to the indicated measure.

radialSmoothCutoff R x is the fixed function S(2-abs(norm(x)/R)), where S is Mathlib Real.smoothTransition. This is the fixed radial cutoff, not a quantified arbitrary family; only positive radii n+1 occur.

Real.log is the totalized real logarithm, with value0 at0. The real function q*log(q) is continuous at0. The subtraction in the displayed type is the literal homogeneous square-entropy formula, without a hidden normalization of mu.

domains.original: Any complete real inner-product/Borel space and any measure; no finite dimension, finite measure, probability or positive mass.
domains.evidence: FiniteDimensional is introduced only after cutoff_integral_limits. Cutoff smoothness/derivative bounds work in general Hilbert spaces; compact support is not used here. The generic Test likewise has no finite-dimensional binder.

quantifiers.reconstructed: Same universal data and conjunction of three natural-index limits.

assumptions.original: Global C2 f; f and true gradient in L2(mu); Phi(f squared) integrable.

conclusion.original: Integrals of f_n squared, Phi(f_n squared), and ||gradient f_n|| squared tend to their uncut integrals.
conclusion.reconstructed: Exactly those three real integral limits, not merely pointwise convergence.
conclusion.evidence: Separate DCT applications use f squared, |Phi(f squared)|+f squared, and 2||gradient f|| squared+2K squared f squared. The gradient limit is proved by local eventual equality. The output is hm AND hp AND he.

scopes.original: Canonical analytic limits for actual C2 representatives, including zeros; not by themselves an LSI or full source exercise.
scopes.reconstructed: Real Bochner integrals, total real log, Phi(0)=0, and genuine Riesz gradient.
scopes.evidence: True L1 envelopes justify all integrals used. Phi is continuous at zero; log continuity at zero and mass division are not invoked. No separable-Hilbert assumption is needed: real-valued integrands are continuous and gradient-L2 supplies its own measurability.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.Cutoff
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DominatedConvergence
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.L2Space
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.NegMulLog
import Mathlib.Topology.Order.OrderClosed

/-!
# Radial cutoff limits and the smooth log-Sobolev test domain

The measure-generic C2 cutoff proof is canonically extracted from
`GaussianLogSobolev`, preserving its complete-Hilbert scope. The new domain
extension applies a compact-C-infinity function LSI to actual compact smooth
approximants, then passes mass, entropy and genuine gradient energy to the limit.

This expands an omitted analytic step in Chewi, *Log-Concave Sampling*
(August20 2026), Section2.1.1, printed48-49/PDF60-61. It is not canonical
probability KL/Fisher, Poincare, a form-domain theorem or full Exercise1.7.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped Topology RealInnerProductSpace ContDiff

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.LogSobolevCutoff
open Analysis.Calculus.Cutoff

private theorem entropy_dilation_bound {a q : ℝ}
    (ha : a ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) (hq : 0 ≤ q) :
    |(a*q) * Real.log (a*q)| ≤ |q * Real.log q| + q := by
  have hmul : (a*q) * Real.log (a*q) =
      a * (q * Real.log q) + q * (a * Real.log a) := by
    have h := Real.negMulLog_mul a q
    simp only [Real.negMulLog_eq_neg] at h
    linarith
  have hab : |a * Real.log a| ≤ 1 := by
    apply abs_le.mpr
    constructor
    · have h := Real.self_sub_one_le_mul_log ha.1
      linarith [ha.1]
    · exact (Real.mul_log_nonpos ha.1 ha.2).trans zero_le_one
  rw [hmul]
  calc
    |a * (q * Real.log q) + q * (a * Real.log a)|
        ≤ |a| * |q * Real.log q| + |q| * |a * Real.log a| := by
          simpa only [abs_mul] using abs_add_le (a * (q * Real.log q)) (q * (a * Real.log a))
    _ ≤ 1 * |q * Real.log q| + q * 1 := by
      rw [abs_of_nonneg ha.1, abs_of_nonneg hq]
      exact add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ha.2 (abs_nonneg _))
        (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hab hq)
    _ = |q * Real.log q| + q := by ring

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

omit [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] in
private theorem gradient_mul (c f : E → ℝ) (x : E)
    (hc : DifferentiableAt ℝ c x) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
    gradient (fun y => c y * f y) x =
      c x • gradient f x + f x • gradient c x := by
  simp only [gradient, fderiv_fun_mul hc hf, map_add, map_smul]

omit [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] in
private theorem cutoff_energy_bound (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f)
    {R C : ℝ} (hR : 1 ≤ R) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hb : ∀ x : E, ‖fderiv ℝ (radialSmoothCutoff R : E → ℝ) x‖ ≤ C / R)
    (x : E) :
    ‖gradient (fun y => radialSmoothCutoff R y * f y) x‖^2 ≤
      2 * ‖gradient f x‖^2 + 2 * C^2 * (f x)^2 := by
  have hRp : 0 < R := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hR
  have hc := (radialSmoothCutoff_contDiff (E := E) hRp).differentiable
    (WithTop.coe_ne_zero.mpr WithTop.top_ne_zero)
  rw [gradient_mul _ _ x (hc x) (hf.differentiable (by norm_num) x)]
  have hcg : ‖gradient (radialSmoothCutoff R : E → ℝ) x‖ ≤ C := by
    change ‖(InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm
      (fderiv ℝ (radialSmoothCutoff R : E → ℝ) x)‖ ≤ C
    rw [(InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm.norm_map]
    exact (hb x).trans (div_le_self hC hR)
  have hcc := radialSmoothCutoff_mem_Icc R x
  have hn : ‖radialSmoothCutoff R x • gradient f x +
      f x • gradient (radialSmoothCutoff R : E → ℝ) x‖ ≤
        ‖gradient f x‖ + C * |f x| := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖radialSmoothCutoff R x • gradient f x‖ +
          ‖f x • gradient (radialSmoothCutoff R : E → ℝ) x‖ := norm_add_le _ _
      _ ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ + C * |f x| := by
        simp only [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hcc.1]
        have h1 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcc.2 (norm_nonneg (gradient f x))
        have h2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcg (abs_nonneg (f x))
        nlinarith
  have hs := (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (by positivity :
    0 ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ + C * |f x|)).mpr hn
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (‖gradient f x‖ - C * |f x|), sq_abs (f x)]

omit [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] in
private theorem cutoff_gradient_eventually_eq (f : E → ℝ) (x : E) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      gradient (fun y => radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) y * f y) x = gradient f x := by
  have hR : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n:ℝ)+1) atTop atTop :=
    tendsto_atTop_add_const_right atTop (1:ℝ) tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
  filter_upwards [hR.eventually (eventually_gt_atTop (‖x‖ + 1))] with n hn
  apply Filter.EventuallyEq.gradient_eq
  refine Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.mpr ⟨1, zero_lt_one, ?_⟩
  intro y hy
  have hb : ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖y-x‖ := by
    calc
      ‖y‖ = ‖x + (y-x)‖ := by congr 1; abel
      _ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖y-x‖ := norm_add_le _ _
  rw [dist_eq_norm] at hy
  have he : radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) y = 1 :=
    radialSmoothCutoff_eq_one_of_norm_le (by positivity) (by linarith)
  simp only [he, one_mul]

/-- Actual radial cutoff limits of square mass, square-log-square and true-gradient
energy on the C2 analytic domain of an arbitrary measure. This is the canonical
extraction of the existing Gaussian implementation, not a new Gaussian fact. -/
theorem cutoff_integral_limits (μ : Measure E) (f : E → ℝ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (hf2 : MemLp f 2 μ)
    (hgrad2 : MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ)
    (hp : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2)) μ) :
    let fn := fun n : ℕ => fun x : E => radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) x * f x
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂μ)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 * Real.log ((fn n x)^2) ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2) ∂μ)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, ‖gradient (fn n) x‖^2 ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂μ)) := by
  dsimp only
  let χ := fun n : ℕ => (radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) : E → ℝ)
  let fn := fun n : ℕ => fun x : E => χ n x * f x
  have hfn (n : ℕ) : ContDiff ℝ 2 (fn n) :=
    ((radialSmoothCutoff_contDiff (E := E) (by positivity : (0:ℝ)<(n:ℝ)+1)).of_le
      (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (le_top : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ ⊤))).mul hf
  have hχb (n : ℕ) (x : E) := radialSmoothCutoff_mem_Icc ((n:ℝ)+1) x
  have hft (x : E) : Tendsto (fun n => fn n x) atTop (𝓝 (f x)) := by
    have hR : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n:ℝ)+1) atTop atTop :=
      tendsto_atTop_add_const_right atTop (1:ℝ) tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop
    have h := ((radialSmoothCutoff_tendsto_one x).comp hR).mul_const (f x)
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, one_mul] using h
  have im : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2) μ := hf2.integrable_sq
  have ie : Integrable (fun x => ‖gradient f x‖^2) μ :=
    (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm hgrad2.aestronglyMeasurable).mp hgrad2
  have hm : Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂μ)) := by
    apply tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (fun x => (f x)^2)
      (fun n => ((hfn n).continuous.pow 2).aestronglyMeasurable) im
    · intro n
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
      have hb := hχb n x
      have hs : (χ n x)^2 ≤ 1 := by dsimp [χ]; nlinarith [hb.1, hb.2]
      change (χ n x * f x)^2 ≤ (f x)^2
      nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hs (sq_nonneg (f x))]
    · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun x => (hft x).pow 2)
  have hphi : Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, (fn n x)^2 * Real.log ((fn n x)^2) ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2) ∂μ)) := by
    apply tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence
      (fun x => |(f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2)| + (f x)^2)
      (fun n => (Real.Continuous.mul_log ((hfn n).continuous.pow 2)).aestronglyMeasurable)
      (hp.abs.add im)
    · intro n
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs]
      have hb := hχb n x
      have ha : (χ n x)^2 ∈ Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1 :=
        ⟨sq_nonneg _, by dsimp [χ]; nlinarith [hb.1, hb.2]⟩
      change |(χ n x * f x)^2 * Real.log ((χ n x * f x)^2)| ≤ _
      simpa only [mul_pow] using entropy_dilation_bound ha (sq_nonneg (f x))
    · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun x =>
        Real.continuous_mul_log.continuousAt.tendsto.comp ((hft x).pow 2))
  obtain ⟨C,hC,hCb⟩ := radialSmoothCutoff_fderiv_bound (E := E)
  have henergy : Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, ‖gradient (fn n) x‖^2 ∂μ)
      atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂μ)) := by
    apply tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence
      (fun x => 2 * ‖gradient f x‖^2 + 2 * C^2 * (f x)^2)
      (fun n => ((Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.continuous_gradient_of_contDiff_one
        ((hfn n).of_le (by norm_num))).norm.pow 2).aestronglyMeasurable)
      ((ie.const_mul 2).add (im.const_mul (2*C^2)))
    · intro n
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
      exact cutoff_energy_bound f hf (by have h := Nat.cast_nonneg (α := ℝ) n; linarith) hC.le
        (hCb _ (by positivity)) x
    · apply Eventually.of_forall
      intro x
      apply tendsto_const_nhds.congr'
      filter_upwards [cutoff_gradient_eventually_eq f x] with n hn
      change ‖gradient f x‖^2 =
        ‖gradient (fun y => radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) y * f y) x‖^2
      rw [hn]
  exact ⟨hm,hphi,henergy⟩

variable [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

/-- A compact-C-infinity function log-Sobolev inequality extends to the genuine
smooth L2/gradient-L2/entropy-integrable domain. The homogeneous entropy is the
literal real integral formula, including zero mass. No sign of C, probability
normalization or chosen RN score is needed for this conditional extension.
A source consumer must produce these analytic inputs, not assume them anew. -/
theorem logSobolev_of_compact_test (μ : Measure E) (C : ℝ)
    (hcompact : ∀ (v : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ∞ v → HasCompactSupport v →
      (∫ x, (v x)^2 * Real.log ((v x)^2) ∂μ) -
        (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
      2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient v x‖^2 ∂μ)
    (f : E → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) (hf2 : MemLp f 2 μ)
    (hgrad2 : MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ)
    (hentropy : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2)) μ) :
    (∫ x, (f x)^2 * Real.log ((f x)^2) ∂μ) -
      (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
    2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient f x‖^2 ∂μ := by
  let fn := fun n : ℕ => fun x : E => radialSmoothCutoff ((n:ℝ)+1) x * f x
  have hfC2 : ContDiff ℝ 2 f :=
    hf.of_le (WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (le_top : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ ⊤))
  obtain ⟨hm, hp, he⟩ := cutoff_integral_limits μ f hfC2 hf2 hgrad2 hentropy
  have hle (n : ℕ) :
      (∫ x, (fn n x)^2 * Real.log ((fn n x)^2) ∂μ) -
        (∫ x, (fn n x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (fn n x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
      2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient (fn n) x‖^2 ∂μ := by
    apply hcompact (fn n)
    · exact (radialSmoothCutoff_contDiff (by positivity)).mul hf
    · exact (radialSmoothCutoff_hasCompactSupport (by positivity)).mul_right
  exact le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto
    (hp.sub (Real.continuous_mul_log.continuousAt.tendsto.comp hm))
    (he.const_mul (2*C)) (Eventually.of_forall hle)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.LogSobolevCutoff

source.anchor: Section2.1.1 printed48/PDF60 compact smooth inequalities and printed49/PDF61 density omission; Exercise1.7 printed43/PDF55
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi's source test conventions; original ASTIS expansion of the omitted analytic step, not a literal printed standalone theorem or complete exercise answer.

publication_context.statement: Assume the homogeneous function LSI Ent_mu(v²)≤2C integral||gradient v||² for every compact C-infinity test on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space. Then it holds on every C-infinity f with actual f/gradient L2 and integrable f² log(f²), with the same C. The proof constructs compact smooth cutoffs and uses actual mass, entropy-integrand and genuine-gradient energy limits. Those limits themselves retain arbitrary-measure C2 complete-Hilbert scope without finite dimension. Analytic inputs are a canonical lemma's domain, not new premises for the final source exercise.
assumptions: The source premise is exactly compact C-infinity LSI, not a stronger compact C2 premise.
The canonical domain explicitly requires true smoothness, f/gradient L2 and entropy integrability; the actual source consumer must derive them.
The literal homogeneous formula, including0 log0=0, is retained. Probability, positive mass, canonical RN score and semigroup domains are not assumed or inferred.

obligations.label: Canonical measure-generic C2 mass/entropy/genuine-gradient limits, extracted without duplicate proof
Extend compact-C-infinity LSI to its actual smooth analytic domain with unchanged constant
Construct the centered source class, normalized entropy and quadratic comparison; uncenter and prove PI/core/form-domain and full exercise

lesson.title: Cutoffs preserve mass, entropy and gradient energy in the limit
lesson.classification: Canonical extraction of an existing generic proof; not new Gaussian mathematics
lesson.statement: Let E be any complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let mu be any measure. Suppose f:E→R is genuinely C2, f and its true gradient belong to L2(mu), and f² log(f²) is integrable. Let chi_R be the existing radial smooth cutoff at radius R, and set f_n=chi_(n+1)*f. Then the integrals of f_n², f_n² log(f_n²), and ||gradient f_n||² converge respectively to those of f², f² log(f²), and ||gradient f||². Finite dimension, probability, finite total measure, positivity and nonzero function mass are not required.
lesson.formula: f_n=\chi_{n+1}f,\qquad \left(\int f_n^2,\ \int\Phi(f_n^2),\ \int\|\nabla f_n\|^2\right)\longrightarrow\left(\int f^2,\ \int\Phi(f^2),\ \int\|\nabla f\|^2\right),\quad\Phi(q)=q\log q,\ \Phi(0)=0.
assumptions: The measure is arbitrary. The three actual analytic domains, not finiteness of mu(E), provide the integrable envelopes. All integrals in the formula are with respect to the same mu.

The gradient is Mathlib's actual Hilbert gradient of the given C2 representative. Its L2 premise includes a.e. strong measurability. A totalized derivative value alone would not establish genuine differentiability.

The cutoff equals1 on the ball of radius R, lies in [0,1], vanishes outside radius2R and has derivative norm at most K/R for one fixed cutoff constant K. In infinite dimension this does not assert compact support; finite dimension enters the later compact-test application, not these limits.

steps.title: Make all approximants measurable
steps.text: The radial cutoff is smooth. Multiplying it by the C2 function gives a C2 approximant, so its square and square-log-square are measurable. The squared norm of its genuine gradient is continuous and real-valued. The assumptions on f and its gradient give the two square integrability inputs.
steps.lean: hfn constructs ContDiff; hf2.integrable_sq and memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm give im and ie. Continuity supplies a.e. strong measurability of the real integrands.

steps.title: Pass the square mass through the integral
steps.text: The cutoff values tend to1, while their absolute values never exceed1. Thus f_n² converges pointwise to f² and is dominated by the already integrable f². Dominated convergence, not pointwise convergence alone, proves the first integral limit.
steps.lean: radialSmoothCutoff_tendsto_one supplies hft. The first tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence invocation uses im as its actual dominator.

steps.title: Control entropy even where the function vanishes
steps.text: Put a=chi_(n+1)² and q=f². The product identity for q log q gives a uniform dilation bound including a=0 and q=0. Its right side is integrable by the entropy and mass hypotheses. Continuity of Phi at zero gives pointwise convergence without assuming that f is nonzero.
steps.lean: The private entropy_dilation_bound proves this scalar estimate from Real.negMulLog_mul. The second DCT uses hp.abs.add im and Real.continuous_mul_log, not continuity of log at zero.

steps.title: Use genuine derivatives and one energy envelope
steps.text: Differentiate the actual product. The cutoff and derivative bounds, with n+1≥1, give one integrable envelope independent of n. No second derivative estimate or integration-by-parts theorem is used.
steps.lean: gradient_mul uses the differentiability premises of fderiv_fun_mul. cutoff_energy_bound transports the derivative norm through the Hilbert Riesz isometry and proves the displayed quadratic estimate.

steps.title: Use local plateaus, then the third dominated limit
steps.text: At each fixed point x, sufficiently large cutoffs equal1 on a neighborhood of x. The gradients of f_n and f are then exactly equal at x. This local fact justifies gradient convergence; convergence of cutoff values by itself would not. The energy envelope from the previous step completes the final DCT.

candidate_assumptions.source: A Euclidean/probabilistic compact-smooth approximation is required before the noncompact test may be used.
candidate_assumptions.lean: Any complete real Hilbert/Borel space and arbitrary measure, C2 f with actual f/gradient L2 and entropy integrability; no finite dimension for limits.

reconstruction.text: For every complete real inner-product normed additive commutative group E equipped with its compatible Borel measurable structure, every measure μ on E, and every function f : E → ℝ, assume that f is globally twice continuously Fréchet differentiable, f and its actual Hilbert gradient ∇f both belong to L²(μ), and x ↦ f(x)² log(f(x)²) is integrable with respect to μ. Here ∇ is the Hilbert Riesz inverse of the real Fréchet derivative, L² membership includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L² seminorm, and integrability includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the absolute value. Let S be the fixed Mathlib Real.smoothTransition and, for each n ∈ ℕ, define f_n(x) = S(2 − |‖x‖/(n+1)|) f(x), equivalently f_n(x) = radialSmoothCutoff(n+1, x) f(x). Then, as n tends to infinity through ℕ, all three limits hold: ∫_E f_n(x)² dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² dμ(x); ∫_E f_n(x)² log(f_n(x)²) dμ(x) → ∫_E f(x)² log(f(x)²) dμ(x); and ∫_E ‖∇f_n(x)‖² dμ(x) → ∫_E ‖∇f(x)‖² dμ(x). Every integral is a real Bochner integral and log is the totalized real logarithm with log(0) = 0. No finite-dimensionality, finiteness of μ, or probability normalization of μ is assumed.
